name: Cham beef sausage
summary: Tung lò mò is the Cham beef sausage of Châu Đốc, dried in strings outside houses, then grilled over charcoal and eaten with rice. A bite brings grilled beef and fat, then sour, sweet, salty, and hot from soy sauce, basil, and pepper.
origin: Cham communities in Châu Đốc. The name comes from the Cham tung lamow, cow gut. Cham Muslims here do not eat pork, so the sausage is beef, and it appears at religious ceremonies.
culture: You see the strings drying in front of houses on the streets away from the center.
taste: Grilled beef and fat first, then sour, sweet, salty, and hot from soy sauce, basil, and pepper.
howToEat: Cut it into rounds, grill them over charcoal until they smell, then cut them smaller and eat them with rice.
Ask for the sour one or the one that is not sour. Dip it in soy sauce.
where: Streets on the outskirts of Châu Đốc, where the sausages hang to dry.
seoTitle: Tung lo mo in Chau Doc
seoDescription: Tung lò mò is the Cham beef sausage of Châu Đốc, dried, grilled over charcoal, and eaten with rice. Sour and not-sour are both sold.
